text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,607.2, down 1.07% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 slipped 0.57%. The move was fairly balanced – advances (251) barely outpaced declines (244) and the breadth score stayed in the “HEALTHY” zone at 62.7, with about two‑thirds of stocks still above their 20‑day moving average. The India VIX fell to 16.55, indicating lower volatility after a modest 2.7% rise over the past five sessions.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added a net ₹1,634.33 cr, extending a 21‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) were net sellers of ₹556.42 cr. FIIs have been net long in index futures (22.1% long) but reduced contracts by 44 03 contracts. Sector‑wise, “Leading” groups such as Realty, Banking, FMCG, Healthcare and IT held the top‑gainer list, whereas “Weakening” areas like PSU Bank, Financial Services and Auto saw more sellers. Options data shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.59 for Nifty, a max‑pain level near 25,700 and support at 25,479, with a call wall at 27,000 and put wall at 25,000.

For the next session watch the Nifty expected range of 25,350.5‑25,863.9 and the key pivot points: support at 25,479 and resistance at 25,822. A break below the 25,479 support could test the 25,000 put wall, while a move above 25,822 may target the 27,000 call wall. Keep an eye on crude oil prices (currently $91.19) and the rupee (₹92.98 per USD), as they have been influencing market sentiment.
